TextEng: You awake to the all-too-familiar sounds of battle and the wet patter of sahuagin feet on the planks above you. For a moment it seems as if you are back aboard the Midnight Rose on the day that she was stolen. Dressing hurriedly, you make for the door... Amidst the cries of your friends and crew, the Skull and Bones lurches suddenly and something clamps against the outside hull. There's the sound of drilling and then of rushing water. Unless you can plug those holes and keep the bilge pump running, the Skull and Bones will quickly sink, crushing you within her hold.

You wake in a cold sweat. The ship was under attack; holes were being drilled in her sides; you and your crew found yourselves overwhelmed by sahuagin. Was it a dream? A premonition of things yet to come? With a sudden sense of deja vu, you hear an urgent knock upon your door...

Sahuagin have attacked the Skull and Bones! Your crew battles bravely on the topdeck while you've been trapped here below, witness to a more sinister plot. The sahuagin have drilled holes in the hull and the water is rushing in. Unless you can plug those holes and keep the bilge pump running, the Skull and Bones will quickly sink, crushing you within her hold.
You've successfully plugged the holes the sahuagin drilled into the hull of the Skull and Bones. Only a few of the foul-smelling beasts remain trapped with you below. It's killing time...

The sahuagin retreat back into the sea, nursing their wounds and leaving a trail of blood behind for the sharks. You can hear your crewmen cheering on the topdeck. They lower a ladder into the hold, eager for you to join.
A Sinking Feeling...

Nisar seems eager to visit Neverwinter's tattoo parlor while on shore leave. He claims that, among the Chultan people, tattoos bring their bearers certain mystical powers. You're not sure if you believe him but, at the very least, it will be a good memento of your time in port.

While on shore leave in Neverwinter, Nisar convinced you to visit the tattoo parlor. He claims that, among the Chultan people, tattoos bring their bearers certain mystical powers. You're not sure if you believe him but you chose the 'Rope & Anchor' tattoo which the tattooist claimed was a mark of willpower.

[+2 Bonus to Will Saves]

While on shore leave in Neverwinter, Nisar convinced you to visit the tattoo parlor. He claims that, among the Chultan people, tattoos bring their bearers certain mystical powers. You're not sure if you believe him but you chose the 'Heart & Arrow' tattoo which the tattooist claimed was a mark of fortitude.

[+2 Bonus to Fortitude Saves]

While on shore leave in Neverwinter, Nisar convinced you to visit the tattoo parlor. He claims that, among the Chultan people, tattoos bring their bearers certain mystical powers. You're not sure if you believe him but you chose what the locals call the 'Neverwinter Eye' tattoo. The tattooist claimed it was a mark of protection.

[+1 Bonus to Armor Class]

While on shore leave in Neverwinter, Nisar convinced you to visit the tattoo parlor. He claims that, among the Chultan people, tattoos bring their bearers certain mystical powers. You're not sure if you believe him but you chose the 'Gnaked Gnome' tattoo which the tattooist swore would improve your reflexes.

[+2 Bonus to Reflex Saves]
Despite Nisar's urgings to the contrary, you left Neverwinter without getting a tattoo. Maybe you can get one at your next port of call.
A Tattoo in Neverwinter

Captain Allendry sent Martins, one of your fellow sailors, to load some cargo from the Silver Sails Trading Company. It's been quite some time, however, and there's still no sign of either Martins or the cargo. Eager to leave harbor, Allendry has ordered you and Nisar to go to the Silver Sails and figure out what's keeping Martins.

Martins, one of your fellow sailors, was in charge of loading a statue from the Silver Sails Trading Company but he left inexplicably before the job was done. Fearful that the statue might be cursed, the superstitious dockworkers refuse to help any further until they know what became of Martins. No doubt he had a sudden alcoholic craving, you muse. You'd better check the local taverns to see if you can find him.

Martins, one of your fellow sailors, was in charge of loading a statue from the Silver Sails Trading Company but he left inexplicably before the job was done. You've found him in the Seedy Tavern but have yet to hear the reason for his departure.

Martins, one of your fellow sailors, was in charge of loading a statue from the Silver Sails Trading Company but he saw a disturbing vision when he brushed against it. He fled the warehouse in fear and took solace in the Seedy Tavern. He refuses to return to duty which means it's up to you and Nisar to return to the Silver Sails and ensure that the statue gets aboard the Midnight Rose.

Despite Martins' panicked departure, you've convinced the superstitious dockworkers at the Silver Sails Trading Company to bring the mysterious statue aboard the Rose. You and Nisar are ready to make your report to Captain Allendry.

Martins' story spooked the superstitious dockworkers at the Silver Sails Trading Company. They've run off, leaving you and Nisar to find a way to get the mysterious statue aboard the Midnight Rose. Rahman Madani, the statue's imperious owner, paces the Silver Sails, deeply angered by the delay. Though he'd never admit it, you suspect he wants to speak with you.

The dockworkers at the Silver Sails Trading Company have run off, leaving you and Nisar to find a way to load Rahman Madani's mysterious statue aboard the Midnight Rose. Rahman suggests levitating the statue aboard and has asked you to retreive his spellbook from his passenger quarters aboard the ship.

You have returned to the Midnight Rose and recovered Rahman Madani's spellbook from his quarters. He's asked you to return it to him so he can levitate his mysterious statue aboard the ship. Captain Allendry gave you an impatient glare as you walked past, so you had best make it quick.

You have given Rahman Madani his spellbook and he will levitate his statue aboard the Midnight Rose as soon as he has had a chance to meditate. You and Nisar are ready to make your report to Captain Allendry.
Loading Cargo
You have found a map in the sand, drawn by the troglodytes who call this desolate island home. The map indicated some sort of sacred cave at the island's southern end.

King Utnal, the troglodyte sovereign, has told you of a sacred cave in the easternmost portion of Troglodyte Island. He has asked you to purge it of his people's Old Gods so that they may convert more easily to the warmblood goddess, Umberlee. If you wish to obey his orders, you will return with the head of whatever god or monster lives within.

A strange and fiery creature greeted you at the entrance to a cave on the island's eastern point, mistaking you for a troglodyte. After telling you to go away, it stuck its tongue out at you and then promptly imploded. Though you consider yourself forewarned, the cave entrance looms before you with nothing to block your way...
You have entered a mysterious cave at the island's eastern tip. Troglodyte corpses line the walls and intricate traps lie scattered about the floor. You'll have to tread carefully.

As it turns out, the mysterious cave at the island's easternmost tip is inhabited by Edgrimm, a stranded dwarven inventor. He's been marooned on this island for goodness knows how long and has clearly gone quite mad as a result. Hopefully you can find your way back to civilization before you share his fate.

As it turns out, the mysterious cave at the island's easternmost tip is inhabited by Edgrimm, a stranded dwarven inventor. He's been marooned on this island for goodness knows how long and has clearly gone quite mad as a result. He's currently trying to build a stone bathysphere in which to escape, a process that will no doubt take years. He has promised to build you a simple raft, however, provided you can bring him the necessary wood.
You have angered Edgrimm and, in his madness, the cave-dwelling dwarven inventor has chosen to attack you.

You angered Edgrimm and, in his madness, the cave-dwelling dwarven inventor attacked you. On his broken body you found some blueprints for something called a Reversible Active Flotation Thingy which just might be your ticket out of here. Gritting your teeth against the meager spray of blood, you cut off Edgrimm's head, tying it to your belt by the beard.

You have stolen the troglodytes' sacred wood and delivered it to the maddened dwarven inventor, Edgrimm. With the help of his illusions, he has built you a Reversible Active Flotation Thingy and urged you not to capsize or set it on fire while at sea.
Of Gods and Monsters

You have stumbled upon Honeypea, your friend from the Blackriver Bandits back in Neverwinter, and she seems eager to join your crew. In the meantime, however, it seems she's busy stealing everything in Spindrift that isn't nailed down. There's one item still missing from her collection, however: an Umberlant relic known as the Scepter of Storms which the priestesses have hidden somewhere within their temple. Honeypea has given you a treasure map that should lead you right to it, provided you can find a way into their Inner Sanctum.

You have found your way into the Temple of Umberlee's Inner Sanctum and, using Honeypea's map, you've been able to recover the coveted Scepter of Storms. If you return it to Honeypea, she'll be sure to join your crew.
You have given Honeypea the Scepter of Storms and she has agreed to join your crew. She'll lay low in the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern until you're ready to set sail.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Honeypea

A talented sailor by the name of Longneck Langer lingers in the jail of Spindrift's pirate governor, waiting to be hung. If you can find a way to free him, you suspect he'd make a fine addition to your crew.

You've met with Longneck Langer in the governor's jail and discussed his alleged crime of 'not being piratey enough.' You have a few ideas as to how to spring him out and can discuss them with him at your leisure.

You've spoken with Governor Blackeye on Longneck Langer's behalf and persuaded him to drop the charges on the condition that you'll take Langer into your crew and teach him to be more piratey. All that's left is to inform Longneck of the good news.
You've spoken with Governor Blackeye and paid a small fortune for Longneck Langer's bail. All that's left is to tell Langer the good news.

You've convinced Falstaff the Tattooist to give Longneck Langer a Jolly Roger Special. He's done an admirable job and Governor Blackeye has dropped all charges of Langer 'not being piratey enough.' After the room clears, Longneck Langer waits behind, eager to offer you his thanks.

Freed from the Governor's jail and spared Jack Ketch's noose, Longneck Langer was quick to join your crew. He awaits your signal in the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern, eager to leave the troubles of Spindrift behind.

Spared Jack Ketch's noose and with some new piratey prostheses to show for it, Longneck Langer was quick to join your crew. He awaits your signal in the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern, eager to set sail and brave the high seas with a blade between his teeth and treasure in the hold.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Longneck Langer
Pegleg Paulson is a regular of the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern and a pirate of some renown. Perhaps he can be convinced to join your crew.

A regular of the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern, Pegleg Paulson has a soft spot for pretty women and a weakness for the sauce. With a few drinks and a coy demeanor, you might be able to convince him to join your crew.

A regular of the Monkey's Cutlass, Pegleg Paulson has a soft spot for pretty women and a weakness for the sauce. Unfortunately, his capacity for both seems a bit limited and now he slumbers drunkenly on the tavern's sawdust floor. Give him a little time to recover and he'll be good as new and eager for more.

A regular of the Monkey's Cutlass, Pegleg Paulson has a soft spot for pretty women and a weakness for the sauce. Using this to your advantage, you've convinced him to join your crew and sail under your command. He'll remain in the Monkey's Cutlass until you give the signal that it's time to weigh anchor.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Pegleg Paulson
There's a fierce minotaur named Redtip running a fight club in the local warehouse. Perhaps you can convince him to join your crew.
There's a fierce minotaur named Redtip running a fight club in the local warehouse. If you can beat him in the ring, he says he'll be glad to join your crew.
You have defeated Redtip the Minotaur in the warehouse fight club, winning his respect. Hopefully he remembers his promise to join your crew.
Redtip the Minotaur has joined your crew and now waits in the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern for your signal to set sail.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Redtip the Minotaur
A talented sailor named Shakey McGuire is recuperating in the local temple after a frightful episode at sea. Perhaps you can convince him to join your crew.

Your attempts to intimidate Shakey McGuire into joining your crew have met with disaster. All you managed to do was scare him even more. He's run away to hide and you doubt he'll ever let you cast eyes on him again.

After calming Shakey McGuire's fears, you've managed to convince him to join your crew. He waits for you in the Monkey's Cutlass, trying to calm his nerves even further with the help of Grogbeard's rum. He'll be ready to sail as soon as you give the signal.

You've taken advantage of Shakey McGuire's fears and bullied him into joining your crew. He waits for you in the Monkey's Cutlass, trying to calm his nerves with the help of Grogbeard's rum. He'll sail as soon as you give the signal.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Shakey McGuire
Sir Francis, a noble and respected privateer, wanders distractedly about the Spindrift warehouse. Perhaps he can be convinced to join your crew.

Sir Francis, a noble and respected privateer, wanders distractedly about the Spindrift warehouse, looking for a lost ring. Perhaps you can learn more from him and ultimately convince him to join your crew.

Sir Francis, a noble and respected privateer, wanders distractedly about the Spindrift warehouse, looking for a lost ring that had been entrusted to him by the notorious scallywag Rascally Pete. The loss of the ring has trapped Sir Francis in a debt of honor from which he cannot escape. Something smells fishy about all of this. You suspect you should seek out Rascally Pete in his home in the sewers and get him to tell you his side of the story...

It's becoming clear to you that, true to his name, the sewer-dwelling Rascally Pete has used false pretenses to ensnare Sir Francis in a debt of honor. The missing ring isn't missing at all but is actually back in Pete's possession, something he's neglected to tell Sir Francis. In order to free Sir Francis from his debt, you'll have to find a way to get the ring back from Rascally Pete...

Your attempt to trick Rascally Pete into giving you the ring that binds Sir Francis in a debt of honor has met with disastrous results. Wise to your ways, Rascally Pete attacked you and now lies dead in his sewer home. That said, you've obtained the contested ring and should now be able to free Sir Francis from his debt, thereby allowing the noble privateer to become a member of your crew.

You have paid Rascally Pete an exorbitant sum of money to free Sir Francis from his debt of honor. Adding salt to the wound, Rascally Pete gave you a curious ring in return - the very same ring that Sir Francis has been searching for all this time. Regardless, what's done is done and Sir Francis should now be free to join your crew.

You have managed to trick Rascally Pete into giving you the ring that binds Sir Francis in a debt of honor. With that in hand, you should now be able to free Sir Francis from his debt, thereby allowing the noble privateer to become a member of your crew.
Freed from his debt of honor to Rascally Pete, Sir Francis has agreed to join your crew. He will wait for your signal in the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Sir Francis
There's a priestess in the temple named Sweetie Marie who seems more interested in lusty pirates than in Umberlee. Perhaps you could convince her to join your crew.

The priestess Sweetie Marie has refused to join your crew, her heart apparently broken by a pirate named Pegleg Paulson who now drowns his sorrows in the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern. Maybe he knows a way to win Sweetie's heart...
You've learned from Pegleg Paulson that the priestess, Sweetie Marie, loved a particular kind of wildflower that grows out by the lighthouse. He's drawn you a treasure map to help you find it.

Thanks to Pegleg Paulson's treasure map, you found some of Sweetie Marie's beloved wildflowers. Perhaps if you give them to her, she'll consider leaving the confines of the temple and joining your crew.

You've won over Sweetie Marie with Pegleg's wildflowers and the pretty young priestess has agreed to join your crew. She's gone to the Monkey's Cutlass to say her goodbyes to Pegleg Paulson and will be ready to set sail whenever you give the signal.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Sweetie Marie
The resident Lighthouse Gnome, Vantabular Garsp, was the first person you met on Spindrift Island. You wonder if he might be interested in joining your crew.

You've invited Vantabular Garsp, Spindrift's resident Lighthouse Gnome, to join your crew and he definitely seemed interested in the idea. First, however, you'll have to help him solve a puzzle left by one of his ancestors and retreive a Garsp family heirloom of some sort. It does sound like quite the challenge...

You have solved the lighthouse puzzle left behind by one of Vantabular Garsp's ancestors and revealed a portal to some mysterious place beyond. A Garsp family heirloom, described as a golden astrolabe, is said to lie within. Retreive it for Vantabular and the Lighthouse Gnome will be more than happy to join your crew.

You have solved the lighthouse puzzle left behind by one of Vantabular Garsp's ancestors and retreived the golden astrolabe that serves as such an important heirloom within the Garsp family tree. In gratitude, Vantabular has agreed to join your crew and has headed to the Monkey's Cutlass to get into more of a sailing mood. He'll be ready to sail whenever you give the sginal.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Vantabular Garsp

Falstaff, owner of the Falstaff's Follies Tattoo Parlor, has run into some sort of trouble with Spindrift's Governor who has imprisoned him until further notice. Until Falstaff can be sprung free of the Governor's jail, the Tattoo Parlor will remain closed.

With your assistance, the sole proprietor of Falstaff's Follies Tattoo Parlor has been sprung from the Governor's jail and his business is back in operation. He seems very talented and you should probably stop by to see what designs he has available.

Falstaff is clearly a tattooist of exceptional talent. You requested a 'Skull & Crossbones' tattoo to serve as a memento of your time in Spindrift and are very happy with how it looks. He assures you it grants a certain resistance to magic.

[Spell Resistance: 12]

Falstaff is clearly a tattooist of exceptional talent. You requested a 'Flaming Skull' tattoo to serve as a memento of your time in Spindrift and are very happy with how it looks. The flames almost seem to flicker in the light, making you feel faster and more dextrous.

[+2 Bonus to Dexterity]

Falstaff is clearly a tattooist of exceptional talent. You requested a 'Waves of Umberlee' tattoo to serve as a memento of your time in Spindrift and are very happy with how it looks. He assures you it has ties to the goddess and the wisdom of her sisterhood.

[+2 Bonus to Wisdom]

Falstaff is clearly a tattooist of exceptional talent.  You requested a 'Dragon's Breath' tattoo to serve as a memento of your time in Spindrift and are very happy with how its copper scales seem to shimmer in the light. He assures you it holds some portion of the dragon's strength.

[+2 Bonus to Strength]
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
A Tattoo in Spindrift

You have stumbled upon Vengaul Bloodsail, the fabled leader of Neverwinter's aging Bloodsailor gang, and he seems eager to join your crew. In the meantime, however, it seems he's busy stealing everything in Spindrift that isn't nailed down. There's one item still missing from his collection, however: an Umberlant relic known as the Scepter of Storms which the priestesses have hidden somewhere within their temple. Vengaul has given you a treasure map that should lead you right to it, provided you can find a way into their Inner Sanctum.

You have found your way into the Temple of Umberlee's Inner Sanctum and, using Vengaul Bloodsail's map, you've been able to recover the coveted Scepter of Storms. If you return it to Vengaul, he'll be sure to join your crew.
You have given Vengaul Bloodsail the Scepter of Storms and he has agreed to join your crew. He'll lay low in the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern until you're ready to set sail.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Vengaul Bloodsail

Spindrift is home to Willigan, a once-famous pirate who sailed with Governor Blackeye in his day. If you can find him, maybe you can convince him to join your crew. Grogbeard, the proprieter of the Monkey's Cutlass Tavern, seems to be the one who knows Willigan the best.

Grogbeard has told you the tragic tale of Whipped Willigan, a once-famous pirate who sailed with Governor Blackeye in his day. He retired young to marry the Governor's daughter but the ballroom beauty soon became a ball and chain. Trapped within his manor house by his shrewish wife and her meddling sisters, Willigan is eager to escape and live the swashbuckling life once more. Grogbeard has signaled Willigan on your behalf, instructing him to put out the ladder they've often used to smuggle rum into Willigan's second-storey study. Go talk to Willigan about this crew of yours and see if there's a way to spring him free.

You've met the tragic figure of Whipped Willigan, a swashbuckling adventurer now cursed and confined by a shrewish wife. Willigan will gladly join your crew if you can smuggle three items back to his room: his Trusty Cutlass, his Pirate Garb, and his Fine Leather Boots. His wife has hidden them on the main floor of their mansion and, together with her sisters, she patrols the hallways diligently. Be careful you don't get caught!

Decked out in his Trusty Cutlass, Pirate Garb, and Fine Leather Boots, Whipped Willigan looks like quite the dashing figure. He leads you downstairs to face his shrewish wife and her meddling sisters once and for all.

Much to Grogbeard's excitement, you rescued his old swashbuckling friend Willigan from a life of soulless matrimony. Willigan has joined your crew and hoists a mug in the Monkey's Cutlass while he awaits your signal to set sail.
As the Skull and Bones pulls out of Spindrift Harbor, you do your best to forget all the business you've left unfinished there. Time is short and you know you have more pressing matters to attend to.
Potential Crewmember: Whipped Willigan

The Midnight Rose has docked briefly in Neverwinter to resupply in preparation for her journey south. Captain Allendry has assigned you some tasks to handle while on shore leave, however. For now, he's asked you to look into some cargo troubles over at the Silver Sails Trading Company.

The Midnight Rose has docked briefly in Neverwinter to resupply in preparation for her journey south. Captain Allendry has assigned you some tasks to handle while on shore leave, however. For now, he's asked you to hurry a last-minute passenger from the Golden Apple.

The Midnight Rose has docked briefly in Neverwinter to resupply in preparation for her journey south. You've completed all of Captain Allendry's tasks and have a small amount of time left to put your affairs in order before the Rose sets sail.
As the Midnight Rose pulls away from Neverwinter's harbor, you cast your mind south to Calimshan. It will be a long journey but it will go faster with the trade winds at your back.
Shore Leave

Old Tom has given you a treasure map of the island, pinpointing the locations of the five sigils where you will leave the crew. Among the other supplies, he also slipped you a strange fetish made of feathers, string, and bone. He refuses to speak of it, however, and bids you on your way. Now that you hold the Sigil Activator, the crewmembers fall in step behind you.

With the aid of the Sigil Activator, you have left a crewmember behind at one of the five sigils marked on Old Tom's map. With each one you leave behind, you can feel the danger grow. You do your best to ration the supplies that Old Tom gave you but you wonder if they will be enough. You keep the strange fetish hidden in your pack, unsure of what to make of it and wary of who might see.

With the aid of the Sigil Activator, you have left a crewmember behind at two of the five sigils marked on Old Tom's map. With each one you leave behind, you can feel the danger grow. You do your best to ration the supplies that Old Tom gave you but you wonder if they will be enough. You keep the strange fetish hidden in your pack, unsure of what to make of it and wary of who might see.

With the aid of the Sigil Activator, you have left a crewmember behind at three of the five sigils marked on Old Tom's map. With each one you leave behind, you can feel the danger grow. You do your best to ration the supplies that Old Tom gave you but you wonder if they will be enough. You keep the strange fetish hidden in your pack, unsure of what to make of it and wary of who might see.

With the aid of the Sigil Activator, you have left a crewmember behind at four of the five sigils marked on Old Tom's map. With each one you leave behind, you can feel the danger grow. You do your best to ration the supplies that Old Tom gave you but you wonder if they will be enough. You keep the strange fetish hidden in your pack, unsure of what to make of it and wary of who might see.

With the aid of the Sigil Activator, you have left your final crewmember behind and all five sigils marked on Old Tom's map have now been activated. Rubbing the strange fetish between your fingers, you make the journey uphill to where Kolmarr awaits your presence.

Kolmarr has passed through the portal that has opened atop the Isle of the Dead and you have little choice but to follow. Old Tom's fetish is growing warm within your hand and you wonder what strange game is being played out between master and servant in this place...
Sigils of the Damned

With a mix of joy and horror, you've learned that the Midnight Rose is docked right here in Spindrift Harbor and that your clumsy raft has led you straight to Lady Tasina's home port. You wonder what it would take to steal back your former ship.

You've found the Midnight Rose in harbor and had a look about. Lady Tasina and her sahuagin crew took good care of her at least. You'll need two things to steal back the Rose, however: a full crew and calmer seas. Outside the safety of the harbor, the gale-force winds would tear her sails right from her mast.

The Midnight Rose lies at anchor in Spindrift Harbor, ripe like a plum for the plucking. You've gathered enough of a crew to steal and sail her, should it come to that, but there's little point until the storms cease and calmer seas prevail. Outside the safety of the harbor, the current gale-force winds would tear her sails right from her mast...

High Preistess Tasina and her fellow Umberlant Sisters have fled Spindrift aboard the Midnight Rose, charting their hellbent course to Fiddler's Green... The storms have cleared but you'll have to find some other ship to pursue the Rose.
Stealing the Midnight Rose

You've been marooned on a tropical island and all of your supplies lie on the bottom of the sea. You will have to craft your own tools if you are to survive but your first priority is to lay claim to a sheltered cave somewhere and find some way to light a fire.
You have found a sheltered cave and the remains of an old firepit but you will have to find a way to light a fire if you intend to keep the night's predators at bay.

You have found a sheltered cave and lit a fire in the firepit to cook food and keep predators at bay. Now that your most pressing needs are met, you begin to wonder what other tools you might be able to craft. You know that you'll need a torch if you intend to explore the island safely.

You have found a sheltered cave, lit a fire in the firepit, and made a torch so you can explore the island more safely. Now that your most pressing needs are met, you begin to wonder what other tools you might be able to craft.

As Troglodyte Island fades into the darkness behind you, all your worries about raw survival fade away. You spy the beam of a lighthouse on the far horizon and are confident that you'll find your way back to civilization before the night is through.
Survivor

Despite the urgency of your quest to catch the Rose, Captain Kolmarr has insisted on a detour to this mist-shrouded place he calls the Isle of the Dead. Apparently some vital artifact lies buried here and Kolmarr insists it will be of value in your coming battle against Umberlee. He waits at the gangplank to explain what must be done.

Kolmarr has explained the nature of the ritual by which he hopes to uncover this artifact that he claims will be of assistance against Umberlee. There are a series of five ancient sigils etched at various points about the island. A crewmember will be left behind at each of them in order to activate them at the proper time. At that point, a portal should open where Kolmarr will be waiting atop the hill. You'll enter together and then seize the artifact from those who have been left behind to protect it. Old Tom has a map indicating the location of all five sigils, a device to activate the sigils, and some supplies to aid against the undead who call this island home. Obtain them from him and the rest of the crew will follow.

At long last, you and your crewmembers have activated all five of the sigils scattered about the Isle of the Dead. Captain Kolmarr waits for you at the top of the hill where a portal will lead the two of you to the ancient artifact that he promises will be of assistance against Umberlee.

Captain Kolmarr has betrayed you and the artifact he promised you has turned the entire crew, yourself included, into ravenous undead. For some reason, however, you managed to maintain your reasonable faculties. Perhaps it had something to do with the strange fetish Old Tom slipped you when he handed you the map... Regardless, now's not the time to ponder such anomalies. Deathly magic now binds your former crew to the necromancer, Kolmarr, and he grows angry at your mutinous behavior.

You have defeated the treacherous necromancer, Kolmarr, and freed your former crew from his nefarious command.
